Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0001] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When a repo has a dedicated money helper (e.g. ledgerly.money.round_money), route every monetary result through it rather than relying on Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
[ace-0003] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Before implementing, read the module's existing helpers and sibling functions (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) to mirror their conventions for conversion (to_money), rounding, and zero handling.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0002] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: For weighted-average or division-based money computations, round only the final result with the project's money helper; do not round intermediate sums, and return the project's ZERO constant for empty/zero-denominator cases.

item.content: When validating integer inputs, explicitly reject bool (isinstance(x, bool)) since bool is a subclass of int; also reject non-int types like float before comparing.

Mirror the error codes and message formats used by sibling functions (e.g. invalid_state with f"invoice {id} is {status}") so new validation paths stay consistent with the codebase's BillingError conventions.

Don't assume round_money/to_money accepts arbitrary types silently; verify behavior with edge inputs (floats, strings) and rely on the helper to raise the project's error (e.g. float_amount) rather than duplicating type checks.
